behavior: Moves deliberately along branches, gleaning insects and spiders from foliage, bark, and twigs; also makes short flights to catch airborne insects. Usually forages from eye level into the canopy and may join mixed-species flocks outside the breeding season.
field_marks: White cheeks bordered by a black mustache stripe
Black streaking across the back and flanks
Two bold white wing bars on long, pointed wings
Small, thin, pointed bill and dark eye
Orange-yellow legs and a short tail
habitat: Breeds chiefly in boreal spruce and tamarack forest, young evergreen stands, and alder or willow thickets. During migration it uses scrub, evergreen forest, and deciduous woodland; in winter it occupies forest edges, second-growth woodland, and wooded canopy.
